summary: Mon Sep 21 06:30:24 PDT 2026 — The branch rewrites README voice and prompt documentation, adds extensive comments and docstrings in prompts.ts, voice.ts, and orchestrate.ts, and adds test prose plus a captured-answer fixture note. Five living-text sentences are false: two reader-facing/frame comments overgeneralize past FAILURE_NOTICE, the wire-record table omits provenance notices, the answering prompt overstates quotation-mark enforcement inside quotations, and the lexer docstring claims totality while its own UTF-16 limit lets astral quotation ornaments pass as prose.

findings.title: Wire table omits provenance text in streamed tokens
findings.sentence: | `streamed_tokens` | Text for the reader — either the generated answer, or the fixed deferral |
findings.claim: The row says streamed_tokens carries only generated answer text or the fixed deferral. The branch adds a refusal path that yields PROVENANCE_NOTICE as a streamed_tokens record, so the exhaustive either/or description is false.
findings.suggestion: | `streamed_tokens` | Text for the reader — generated answer text, the fixed deferral, or the provenance notice |

findings.title: Prompt overstates quotation-like mark enforcement
findings.sentence: An answer containing one is stopped.
findings.claim: The prompt says an answer containing any other quotation-like mark is stopped. Inside an outer curly quotation the lexer treats such marks as the record's own content; after verification the streaming path emits the whole raw quotation rather than refusing it.
findings.suggestion: An answer using one outside a quotation is stopped; inside a quotation it is the record's own content.

findings.title: Frame comment overgeneralizes to every reader-facing notice
findings.sentence:
The frame as a reader sees it: the one wording the answer path injects and every
 * reader-facing notice opens with.
findings.claim: The comment says every reader-facing notice opens with DISPLAY_FRAME. FAILURE_NOTICE is in READER_FACING_PROMPTS and deliberately begins with neutral infrastructure prose rather than the avatar frame.
findings.suggestion: The frame as a reader sees it: the one wording the answer path injects and the avatar-voiced notices open with.

findings.title: Reader-facing list comment includes a neutral notice
findings.sentence:
The prompts a reader actually meets — the avatar's own voice, finished rather
 * than provisional.
findings.claim: The comment characterizes the whole reader-facing list as the avatar's own voice. The list includes FAILURE_NOTICE, whose own docstring says it is deliberately not in character and whose text is neutral infrastructure prose.
findings.suggestion: The prompts a reader actually meets; the avatar-voiced ones are finished, while `FAILURE_NOTICE` is deliberately neutral.

findings.title: Lexer docstring claims totality despite its stated astral limit
findings.sentence:
Every other mark that could pass for a delimiter is a **violation**, so the
 * grammar is total over quotation marks rather than letting an unrecognised one
 * through as prose: a straight `"` anywhere outside a quotation (it is not
 * directional, so it cannot nest), a closing `”` with nothing open, `‘` anywhere
 * (it can only open), and `'` or `’` where a word starts.
findings.claim: The sentence says the grammar is total and lets no unrecognised quotation mark through as prose. The same branch's stated UTF-16 limit says the astral quotation ornaments 🙶🙷🙸 pass as prose, directly contradicting the totality claim.
findings.suggestion: Every other mark the lexer can match that could pass for a delimiter is a violation; marks stored as two UTF-16 units are the stated exception and pass as prose.
